newsitem.title: USA: Bonneville offers no power Saturday through Monday.
newsitem.headline: Bonneville offers no power Saturday through Monday.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) offered no power for pre-scheduled sales Saturday through Monday, the federal agency said Friday.
For Friday's pre-schedulings, BPA offered up to 200 megawatts (MW) for firm sales during both light- and heavy-load hours. Up to 200 MW were also offered for non-firm, light-load hours on Friday.
BPA's previous offer for firm power during heavy-load hours was $25.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) in the Northwest and $26.50 for California-Oregon (COB) and Nevada-Oregon (NOB) border deliveries.
The federal power marketing agency had also offered firm power during light load hours on Friday at $19.50 for both the Northwest and COB/NOB.
BPA's previous offer for non-firm power during off-peak hours was $18.50 to $20.00 per MWh.

Industry sources have said Northwest hydroelectric generation will likely decline over the weekends until late November, as flows are reduced so that fisheries experts can take stock of fish nest progress.
